subject.title: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals

question: Should the canonical implementation use one authoritative deny-policy store and force human one-shot approval ahead of full/off, allowlist hits, and durable trust across every execution host?
rationale: This changes a stable core authorization boundary, and the active implementation currently leaves persisted ownership and permanent override semantics to maintainer intent.

options.title: Single-owner approval overlay
options.body: Store rules in one canonical approvals-policy surface and require a human one-shot decision for every match across gateway, node, and companion paths.

options.title: Dual persisted sources
options.body: Support both configuration files with explicit union, precedence, migration, UI synchronization, and upgrade guarantees.

options.title: Hard-deny matches
options.body: Treat every deny-pattern match as an absolute denial without a human override.

recommendation.title: Single-owner approval overlay
recommendation.body: Store rules in one canonical approvals-policy surface and require a human one-shot decision for every match across gateway, node, and companion paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The long-term central-file history and prior issue discussion make this the strongest available owner for the permanent exec authorization policy.
